extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers (particularly women, parents, and those interested in healthful clothing)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance on selecting, arranging, and wearing clothing to promote bodily health across ages and seasons — covering mechanical support, materials, ventilation, color, dyes, and cleanliness. Draws on observations, prison weighings, and practical rules for seasonal timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footwear: heel and arch design
rubrics_metrics.description: The heel should not be raised from the ground beyond the level of the palm of the foot; the arch ought always to have full play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the heel is raised the plan of the arch is deranged and the elastic, wave-like motion of the foot impeded. Mr. Dowie's plan of introducing an elastic connection or band across the arch, so as to allow it freedom, is commended as an admirable device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support clothes by the shoulders, not the waist
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax of carrying clothes from the waist is utterly unjustifiable; the parts that should bear the burden are the shoulders and none other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carrying heavy robes from the waist layers upon layer causes a burden comparable to corsets; the corset sometimes exists only to shield the body from those bands. Women should be placed under the same favorable conditions for movement as men by moving support to the shoulders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid heavy, trailing garments
rubrics_metrics.description: When dresses are long, trail on the ground, and are made of heavy material, the weight and incumbrance are drags on the life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such garments impose a burden that even the strongest man could not sustain in ordinary activity; prefer lighter textures or carry weight on shoulders rather than waist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve feminine outer robe while adapting support
rubrics_metrics.description: The flowing robe which even trespasses a little on the ground is most graceful and characteristic of feminine beauty and should remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain graceful outer appearance but, insofar as health, warmth, freedom of movement, and the mode by which the dress is carried are concerned, women should have the same practical improvements (shoulder support, even covering) that benefit men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child dress — allow active play and full coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let her have no stays, and let her run about like the boys." Girls should be clothed cap-a-pie and well clothed from head to foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dress girls like boys (e.g., knickerbockers) with lighter under-garments and an outer gown to distinguish sex while permitting free movement; this prevents misshapenness and supports health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover the throat in cold months
rubrics_metrics.description: The throat should be covered during the period extending from October to April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The throat is a common part to become affected during cold weather; observations show those with uncovered throats more often have throat affections and colds. Adequate moderate covering of the throat reduces deleterious effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head coverings: light, free, and ventilated
rubrics_metrics.description: Head coverings should always be light and free, whether bonnet, cap, or hat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer hats that are ventilated (e.g., gypsy hat, Geneva/Leonardo da Vinci cap). Avoid close-fitting felt hats and heavy stiff hats; a light, well-ventilated tall hat is healthier than an unventilated one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate clothing seasonally (timing guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulate the amount and kind of clothing worn at different periods of the year; when the body requires more food and sleep to meet the cold, it requires more clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed periodicity in weight and metabolism (Milner and Smith) to guide practice: be warmest clothed from end of January to end of February; do not assume summer dress until about May 15; adopt winter clothing by November 1 and continue beyond the turning of the season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation: avoid extremes of exposure and over-wrapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Extremes on both sides (hardening by exposure vs. over-encumbering with clothes) are bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some individuals flourish with exposure but are exceptional; many (especially children and the aged) suffer if under-clad. Conversely, stout persons often over-wrap when they need less protection. Apply common sense to balance protection and hardening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underclothing material: silk next to skin, wool over it
rubrics_metrics.description: For underclothing a decided preference is given to silk, worn next to the skin; over the silk there should be a woolen covering for most of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silk best maintains warmth, affords lightness, and transmits perspiration; though expensive, its durability offsets cost. Wool coverings should not be thick heavy flannel but soft, light, fleecy material or thin flannel resembling silk. Feet coverings likewise should be light and warm; long socks preferred to stockings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer garment fit and choice for cold
rubrics_metrics.description: The final overcoat or cloak should fit loosely to the body; in coldest weather fur is the best external clothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outer clothing should vary with season; loose fit allows ventilation and freedom of movement while providing warmth; fur recommended in extreme cold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventilation of clothes; cautious use of waterproofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain free ventilation of clothes — whatever impedes evaporation of water from the body leads to derangement or disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained moisture saturates garments producing chilliness and checking skin action, leading to cold, dyspepsia, or rheumatism. Waterproofs are dangerous when exercising because they trap the body's own moisture while being chilled externally; use waterproofs only when at rest. For active exercise a good large umbrella is preferable to waterproofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color of dress: light or gray preferred; avoid black
rubrics_metrics.description: Light-colored dress is at once the warmest and the healthiest; gray is the best compromise for general wear; black outer suits are inconvenient and unwholesome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Light colors are negative to cold (do not absorb heat) and are appropriate even in Arctic analogies; white shows dirt quickly (which can be advantageous), so gray combines health and practicality. Black outer garments (and heavy black mourning clothes) are criticized as unhealthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid poisonous dyes; rinse colored garments
rubrics_metrics.description: Aniline dye stuffs (red or yellow coralline) sometimes caused local irritation and occasional constitutional derangement when in contact with the skin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symptoms include raised eruption of minute pimples, local pain, vesicles with watery discharge; remove colored garments causing irritation and do not wear them until they have been many times rinsed in boiling water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness of dress
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean clothes are essential to health; health will not be clad in dirty raiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dirty clothing causes minor ailments (oppression, dullness, headache, nausea) that materially lower standards of health. There is a need for accessible well-washed clothes and public laundries to enable cleanliness in large centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing should allow free breathing, circulation, and avoid digestive pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothing should give free motion to breathing and circulation, make no undue pressure on the digestive organs, leave the limbs free, be easily put on and off, and allow ready change with weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Men's modern attire exemplifies these advantages (equal coverage, borne by shoulders); these functional benefits should be faithfully copied for women to promote health while retaining outward grace.
